original_sentence: Friendship on the rocks: please advise!
readingExamples: Friendship on the rocks: please advise!
definitionEn:
(1) phr. (of a relationship, marriage or business) experiencing serious difficulties and likely to fail or collapse soon
(2) phr. (of a ship) run aground on rocks and wrecked
(3) phr. (of a drink, especially whisky) served with ice cubes but without water

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (酒)加冰块的(常见于餐饮场景,如 whisky on the rocks)
uncommonMeanings.example: The old sailor sat alone at the bar, a whisky on the rocks melting slowly in front of him, his weathered eyes fixed on a photograph no one else could see. （读后续写·人物刻画·孤独氛围）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (船)触礁搁浅;失事
uncommonMeanings.example: By dawn the fishing boat lay on the rocks, its hull torn open by the reef, yet the whole crew had somehow made it ashore alive. （读后续写·海难脱险·环境描写）

posExamples.sentence: Ever since the misunderstanding over the borrowed diary, our once-inseparable friendship had been on the rocks, and every awkward silence in class reminded me of what we had lost. （读后续写·友谊裂痕·心理描写）
I am writing to seek your advice because my friendship with my closest classmate seems to be on the rocks, and I have no idea how to mend the growing distance between us. （应用文·求助信）
When a relationship appears to be on the rocks, running away is never the answer; only honest communication and a willingness to forgive can steer it back to calmer waters. （议论文·人际交往·比喻论证）
The small family bookshop had been on the rocks for months, yet the moment neighbours heard the news, they rushed in to buy, determined not to let a piece of their childhood disappear. （读后续写·社区温情·转折）

idioms.translation: (关系、计划)遭遇严重挫折,濒临破裂
idioms.example: Their partnership hit the rocks when neither side was willing to admit a single mistake — pride, not distance, had become the real enemy. （议论文·合作与包容·例证）

idioms.idiom: run onto the rocks / go on the rocks
idioms.translation: 触礁;(事业、婚姻)走向失败
idioms.example: Just when the young couple's marriage seemed about to go on the rocks, the arrival of their first child reminded them of the promise they had once made. （读后续写·家庭·转折）

collocations.phrase: a relationship / marriage on the rocks
collocations.example: To an outsider they looked like the perfect couple, but behind closed doors their marriage had long been on the rocks. （读后续写·人物反差）
A friendship on the rocks is not necessarily a friendship over; sometimes a single sincere apology is all it takes to set things right. （议论文·友谊·辩证观点）

collocations.phrase: put / drive sth on the rocks
collocations.example: Constant jealousy and endless comparison had slowly driven their once-warm bond on the rocks. （读后续写·情感恶化）

collocations.phrase: whisky / a drink on the rocks
collocations.example: "A whisky on the rocks, please," he said, loosening his tie after the longest day of his life. （读后续写·人物细节·情绪释放）
With patience and honesty on both sides, a relationship can often be brought back from the rocks stronger than before. （议论文·修复关系）
With his family business on the rocks, the young man swallowed his pride and asked his former rival for help. （读后续写·励志转折·人物成长）

synonyms.example: The moment I saw her red eyes, I knew our friendship was in trouble, and that pretending otherwise would only make things worse. （读后续写·察觉危机）
synonyms.usage: in trouble 为最通用的口语表达,泛指各种困境;on the rocks 更形象生动,专指关系、婚姻、事业濒临破裂

synonyms.example: As misunderstandings piled up like autumn leaves, our friendship was quietly falling apart, and neither of us dared to speak first. （读后续写·关系瓦解·比喻）
synonyms.usage: falling apart 强调'逐渐瓦解'的动态过程,可用于关系、计划、人的精神状态;on the rocks 强调已到'触礁'的危险临界点

synonyms.example: Communication between the two teams had completely broken down, and the project ground to a halt. （议论文·团队协作·因果论证）
synonyms.usage: break down 侧重系统、机制、沟通的'崩溃失灵';on the rocks 是形象习语,专用于关系、婚姻、生意等即将失败的语境

advancedExpressions.expression: what had once been ... was now on the rocks, until ...
advancedExpressions.example: What had once been the warmest friendship in our class was now on the rocks, until a single note slipped into my desk — "I miss you" — melted three months of stubborn silence. （今昔对比+悬念细节,标记情感拐点）

advancedExpressions.expression: my ... seems to be on the rocks, and I would be grateful for any advice on how to ...
advancedExpressions.example: My friendship with my deskmate seems to be on the rocks, and I would be truly grateful for any advice on how to rebuild the trust we have lost. （求助信·委婉陈述困境+明确诉求）

advancedExpressions.expression: a relationship on the rocks can still be steered back to safe waters if ...
advancedExpressions.example: A relationship on the rocks can still be steered back to safe waters if both sides are willing to let understanding, rather than pride, hold the wheel. （航海隐喻贯穿始终,pride/understanding 对比升华）

sentenceUpgrade.original: My friendship with her was in trouble.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The friendship I had treasured for years was suddenly on the rocks, and every unanswered message felt like another wave hammering against a boat I no longer knew how to steer. （读后续写·航海隐喻+心理描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: on the rocks 习语替换 in trouble + wave hammering 延续航海意象 + a boat I no longer knew how to steer 外化无助感

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not give up when a relationship has problems.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: When a relationship drifts on the rocks, the wise choice is not to abandon ship but to reach for the oar of honest communication and row, patiently, back towards each other. （议论文·比喻论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: drift on the rocks/abandon ship/oar/row 航海隐喻链 + not to...but to 对比句式 + patiently 副词点睛

translation: 局促不安的；令人尴尬的；难对付的；笨拙的
original_sentence: When I was an awkward primary school student, she was the popular girl who was willing to make friends with me.
readingExamples: When I was an awkward primary school student, she was the popular girl who was willing to make friends with me.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. making you feel embarrassed, uncomfortable or self-conscious in a social situation
(2) adj. difficult to deal with or handle; causing problems and requiring skill or care
(3) adj. not moving in a smooth or graceful way; clumsy in movement or manner
(4) adj. (of a person) deliberately unhelpful or difficult to please

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (处境、问题)棘手的,难对付的(而非'尴尬')
uncommonMeanings.example: The teacher's simple question put me in an awkward position: telling the truth would betray a friend, yet a lie would betray myself. （读后续写·道德两难·心理描写）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (时间、位置)不方便的,别扭的
uncommonMeanings.example: The meeting was scheduled at an awkward hour, right in the middle of the afternoon nap that Grandpa never gave up. （读后续写·生活细节·幽默）

posExamples.sentence: As an awkward new student who knew no one, I hovered at the edge of the noisy playground, until a girl with a bright smile walked over and simply said, "Come sit with us." （读后续写·校园破冰·环境与心理）
If you feel awkward speaking English in front of the whole class, our English corner offers a relaxed and friendly place where making mistakes is not only allowed but welcomed. （应用文·社团招募）
Feeling awkward in an unfamiliar setting is not a weakness but a natural stage of growth; the moment we dare to speak first, awkwardness quietly turns into confidence. （议论文·成长与勇气·观点论证）
An awkward silence fell over the dinner table after my careless remark, and I watched Mum's smile fade like sunlight behind a passing cloud. （读后续写·家庭冲突·比喻）

idioms.example: After his joke fell flat, an awkward silence hung in the room until the shy new boy suddenly laughed, and the ice was broken at last. （读后续写·社交破冰）
His unexpected question put me in an awkward position, torn between loyalty to my friend and honesty to my teacher. （读后续写·道德抉择）

idioms.translation: 青春期尴尬的年纪;青涩年华
idioms.example: At the awkward age of thirteen, everything about myself seemed wrong — too tall, too quiet, too easily embarrassed. （读后续写·青春成长·自我怀疑）

collocations.example: I felt so awkward standing alone at the party that I pretended to be absorbed in my phone, wishing I could simply melt into the wall. （读后续写·社交焦虑·动作细节）
An awkward pause followed her confession, and for a heartbeat neither of them knew whether to laugh or cry. （读后续写·情感场景）
Learning to handle awkward situations with grace is a skill that will serve you far beyond the school years. （议论文·情商与成长）
There was an awkward moment when I called my new teacher by the wrong name, but her warm laughter instantly set me at ease. （读后续写·校园幽默）
The reporter's awkward question left the young champion silent for a long moment before she answered with unexpected honesty. （读后续写·人物刻画）
At first I felt awkward about asking for help, but I soon learned that admitting weakness is itself a kind of strength. （议论文·成长感悟）
She was passing through that awkward age when a single unkind comment could ruin an entire week. （读后续写·青春敏感）
Rather than making things awkward by refusing outright, she gently explained her reasons and offered a kinder alternative. （应用文·处理人际·委婉表达）

synonyms.example: Cheeks burning, the embarrassed boy stared at his shoes as the whole class turned to look at him. （读后续写·羞窘·动作描写）
synonyms.usage: embarrassed 直接描述人内心'难为情'的情绪;awkward 既可形容人不自在,也可形容气氛、处境、动作,范围更广

synonyms.example: With clumsy fingers he tried to tie the ribbon, but the harder he tried, the more hopelessly it tangled. （读后续写·动作细节）
synonyms.usage: clumsy 专指动作笨拙、不协调;awkward 表'笨拙'时含义相近,但更常用于形容社交尴尬和棘手处境

synonyms.example: She shifted uncomfortably in her seat as the questions grew more and more personal. （读后续写·心理不适）
synonyms.usage: uncomfortable 泛指身体或心理上的'不舒服';awkward 特指因社交场合或处境而产生的'别扭、尴尬'

synonyms.example: Balancing honesty and kindness in a reply is a tricky task that even adults sometimes get wrong. （议论文·人际智慧）
synonyms.usage: tricky 侧重问题'复杂难解、需要技巧';awkward 表'棘手'时更强调因两难或不便而'令人为难'

advancedExpressions.expression: the awkward silence was broken when ...
advancedExpressions.example: The awkward silence was broken when the shyest boy in the room suddenly held out half of his sandwich — a small gesture that turned a stranger into a friend. （以细节动作打破僵局,小善举传情）

advancedExpressions.expression: if you feel awkward about ..., remember that ...
advancedExpressions.example: If you feel awkward about speaking up in class, remember that everyone around you shares the same fear, and the first brave voice is always the one others secretly thank. （建议信·共情+鼓励）

advancedExpressions.expression: far from being a flaw, awkwardness is ...
advancedExpressions.example: Far from being a flaw to be ashamed of, awkwardness is simply the growing pain of a person daring to step beyond the familiar. （far from 否定+隐喻,重新定义概念）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I felt awkward when I met new people.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Whenever I faced a room of unfamiliar faces, an awkward heat would creep up my neck, my carefully rehearsed greetings dissolving into a clumsy, half-swallowed "hi". （读后续写·社交焦虑·生理细节）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: an awkward heat crept up my neck 生理反应外化情绪 + carefully rehearsed...dissolving 反差 + half-swallowed 精准修饰

sentenceUpgrade.original: It is normal for teenagers to feel awkward.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It should be recognized that the awkwardness so common among teenagers is not a defect to be corrected but a bridge every one of us must cross on the way to a more confident self. （议论文·辩证论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It should be recognized that 正式句式 + not...but 对比重新定义 + a bridge...must cross 隐喻升华

original_sentence: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight.
readingExamples: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the ability to see; the power of vision
(2) n. the act of seeing something, or the fact that it can be seen; the range within which something can be seen
(3) n. a thing that is seen; a view or spectacle, especially a remarkable or memorable one
(4) n. (usually plural, sights) places of interest that people visit as tourists

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (常用 a sight)一副糟糕/滑稽的样子;(口语)难看的景象
uncommonMeanings.example: Soaked to the skin and covered in mud, I must have been a sight, yet Grandma only laughed and wrapped me in the warmest towel in the house. （读后续写·祖孙温情·幽默）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (枪炮的)瞄准器,准星
uncommonMeanings.example: The young hunter lined up the deer in his sights, but the moment their eyes met, his finger froze on the trigger. （读后续写·抉择时刻·心理转折）

posExamples.sentence: The train pulled away, and I pressed my face to the window until my hometown finally disappeared from sight, taking a piece of my heart with it. （读后续写·离别·环境与心理）
During the field trip, please stay within sight of your group leader at all times, as the mountain paths can be steep and easy to lose your way on. （应用文·安全须知/通知）
We should never lose sight of the fact that success is measured not only by grades, but by the kindness and courage we show along the way. （议论文·价值观·观点论证）
As we reached the hilltop, the most breathtaking sight unfolded before us — a sea of clouds glowing gold in the first light of dawn. （读后续写·自然风光·景物描写）

wordForms.adjective: sightless (adj. 失明的); sighted (adj. 有视力的)
wordForms.other: sightseeing (n. 观光,游览); sightseer (n. 观光者); insight (n. 洞察力); foresight (n. 远见); eyesight (n. 视力)

idioms.idiom: out of sight, out of mind
idioms.translation: 眼不见,心不烦;久别情疏
idioms.example: People say out of sight, out of mind, yet the friend who moved abroad still writes to me every festival — some bonds simply refuse to fade. （议论文·友谊·反驳论证）
At first sight the old house seemed cold and unwelcoming, but the moment I stepped inside, the smell of fresh bread told a warmer story. （读后续写·反差·细节描写）
For Grandpa it was love at first sight — sixty years on, he still describes the exact dress Grandma wore that spring afternoon. （读后续写·家史温情）

idioms.translation: 看不见;忽视,忘记(重要的事)
idioms.example: In the endless race for higher marks, we must never lose sight of why we began to learn in the first place. （议论文·教育初心）
Just as I was giving up hope, I caught sight of a familiar red umbrella pushing through the crowd — Mum had come for me after all. （读后续写·寻找·转折）

idioms.translation: 令人眼前一亮的人/物;久违的喜人景象
idioms.example: After a week lost in the mountains, the distant lights of the village were a sight for sore eyes. （读后续写·脱险·情感释放）

collocations.example: With the finish line finally in sight, the exhausted runner summoned every last ounce of strength and surged forward. （读后续写·体育励志）
She waved until the bus turned the corner and her mother was out of sight, then wiped her eyes and walked bravely on. （读后续写·离别）
As the fog lifted, a small fishing village came into sight, its red roofs scattered like petals along the quiet shore. （读后续写·景物描写）
Amid all the busy revision, we should not lose sight of the importance of rest and a healthy mind. （议论文·平衡学习与健康）
At the sight of her old diary, a flood of forgotten summers came rushing back, warm and bittersweet. （读后续写·回忆·比喻）
Our foreign friends are eager to see the sights of our ancient city, from the old temple to the moonlit river. （应用文·行程安排）
At first sight the problem looked impossible, but breaking it into smaller steps soon revealed a clear way through. （议论文·解决问题·方法）
The cottage stood in sight of the sea, and every morning we woke to the sound of waves and the cry of gulls. （读后续写·环境描写）
I knew the quiet librarian only by sight, until the day she quietly saved the very book I had dreamed of reading. （读后续写·人物·温情）

synonyms.example: Years of reading in dim light had weakened his vision, yet his imagination remained as sharp and bright as ever. （读后续写·人物·反差）
synonyms.usage: vision 较正式,既指'视力',也常引申为'远见、愿景';sight 更日常,侧重'看见的能力'与'看到的景象'

synonyms.example: From the top floor, the view of the city lights stretched endlessly, and for a moment all my worries seemed very small. （读后续写·景物+心理）
synonyms.usage: view 侧重从某处望出去的'景色'或'观点';sight 侧重某个具体、往往令人印象深刻的'景象'

synonyms.translation: 场景,景象;(事件发生的)现场
synonyms.example: The scene at the railway station moved everyone to tears: soldiers embracing the families they had not seen for years. （读后续写·情感场景）
synonyms.usage: scene 指某个'场面、情景',常含人物活动或情节;sight 更强调纯视觉上'看到的东西'

synonyms.example: The dragon-boat race was a spectacle of colour and thunderous drums that visitors would remember for a lifetime. （应用文·活动介绍）
synonyms.usage: spectacle 特指'盛大、壮观'的场面,感情色彩强;sight 中性,普通景象与壮丽景象皆可用

advancedExpressions.expression: ... until ... finally faded / disappeared from sight
advancedExpressions.example: I stood rooted to the platform, waving and waving, until the little green train finally faded from sight and the silence that followed felt almost unbearable. （动作重复+视觉消退,烘托不舍）

advancedExpressions.expression: we must not lose sight of ...
advancedExpressions.example: While chasing higher scores, we must not lose sight of the true purpose of education — to grow into thoughtful, caring and independent individuals. （建议信·提醒初心）

advancedExpressions.expression: the true goal ... should never slip out of sight
advancedExpressions.example: In an age dazzled by instant success, the true goal of learning — cultivating wisdom rather than merely storing facts — should never slip out of sight. （视觉隐喻+破折号补充,论点鲜明）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I watched him leave until I could not see him.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I watched his figure grow smaller and smaller until it melted into the crowd and vanished from sight, and only then did I realize how much I would miss him. （读后续写·离别·倒装心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: grow smaller and smaller 渐进 + melted into/vanished from sight 视觉消退 + only then did I realize 倒装点出情感

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not forget our original goal.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: However fierce the competition may become, we must never lose sight of the goal that first set us on this journey, for a traveller who forgets the destination will only wander in circles. （议论文·比喻论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: However...may become 让步状语从句 + lose sight of 习语 + a traveller who...隐喻说理

original_sentence: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight.
readingExamples: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. beyond the range of someone's vision; in a place where a particular person cannot see it
(2) phr. away from someone's watchful attention or supervision

posExamples.sentence: The mother did not relax for a single second until the school bus turned the corner and her little son was out of her sight, and even then she stood waving at the empty street. （读后续写·母爱·细节描写）
For safety reasons, young children should never be left out of an adult's sight while playing near the water during the summer camp. （应用文·安全须知）
Real trust means allowing those we love to step out of our sight, confident that the values we have shared will guide them wherever they go. （议论文·信任与放手·观点论证）
The moment the guard was out of my sight, I slipped through the half-open gate, my heart pounding so loudly I feared the whole world could hear it. （读后续写·冒险·心理紧张）

idioms.idiom: out of sight, out of mind
idioms.translation: 眼不见,心不烦;久别情疏
idioms.example: They warned me that friends who move away soon fade — out of sight, out of mind — but a single handwritten letter each month proved them wonderfully wrong. （议论文·友谊·反驳论证）

idioms.translation: 躲开某人的视线,避免被某人看见
idioms.example: The stray puppy learned to keep out of the shopkeeper's sight, waiting in the shadows until a kind hand finally reached out to it. （读后续写·流浪动物·温情）

collocations.example: I chased the balloon down the street until it drifted over the rooftops and vanished out of sight, leaving me with an odd, wordless sadness. （读后续写·童年·怅惘）

collocations.phrase: keep sb / sth out of sight
collocations.translation: 把某人/某物藏起来不让看见
collocations.example: She quickly slid the surprise gift out of sight the moment she heard her brother's footsteps on the stairs. （读后续写·惊喜·动作细节）
"Get out of my sight!" he shouted in the heat of anger — words he would spend the rest of the night wishing he could take back. （读后续写·冲突·悔恨）
The frightened kitten stayed out of sight beneath the old sofa until the gentle voice of the little girl finally coaxed it out. （读后续写·救助动物）

collocations.phrase: be hardly out of sb's sight
collocations.translation: 几乎不离开某人的视线;形影不离
collocations.example: Throughout that unforgettable summer, the two best friends were hardly out of each other's sight, sharing every secret, snack and silly dream. （读后续写·友谊·温情）
Behind his cheerful smile, hidden out of sight, lay a loneliness that only his diary ever came to know. （读后续写·人物内心·反差）

synonyms.example: The little boat slipped quietly out of view behind the misty headland, and the harbour fell strangely still. （读后续写·景物·氛围）
synonyms.usage: out of view 侧重客观'不在视野范围内';out of one's sight 更强调'某个特定的人'看不见,常带情感色彩

synonyms.translation: 在某人够不到/控制不到的地方
synonyms.example: Once her children grew up and moved beyond her reach, the old mother learned the hardest lesson of love: to trust and to let go. （议论文·放手·亲情）
synonyms.usage: beyond one's reach 侧重'触及不到、掌控不了';out of one's sight 侧重'看不见',二者常在'放手'语境中互补

synonyms.translation: 未被看见的,不为人知的
synonyms.example: Countless unseen acts of kindness quietly hold our society together, though they rarely make the headlines. （议论文·善行·观点句）
synonyms.usage: unseen 为形容词,修饰'未被注意到'的事物;out of one's sight 为短语,强调暂时脱离某人的视线

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. did not move / stop ... until ... was out of sight
advancedExpressions.example: Mum did not turn back to the house until the last flicker of my figure was out of sight, and I later learned she had stood there long after the road lay empty. （延迟动作+补叙,双向牵挂）

advancedExpressions.expression: please make sure ... is never out of your sight
advancedExpressions.example: During the outing, please make sure your younger partner is never out of your sight, especially near the lake and the crowded market. （安全须知·祈使句+明确场景）

advancedExpressions.expression: to love someone is to let them step out of our sight and still believe in them
advancedExpressions.example: To love someone truly is to let them step out of our sight and still believe, wholeheartedly, that they will find their own way home. （对'爱'的哲理定义+情感升华）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She watched her son until she could not see him.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: She stood at the gate, her eyes following her son's every step until his small backpack bobbed round the corner and slipped out of her sight, and only then did she let the tears fall. （读后续写·母爱·倒装心理）

translation: 失去，丧失；亏损；去世；损失
original_sentence: The stress of this situation is killing me, and I'm at a loss what to do next.
readingExamples: The stress of this situation is killing me, and I'm at a loss what to do next.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the fact of no longer having something, or of having less of it than before
(2) n. the disadvantage caused when someone leaves or when a useful or valuable object is taken away
(3) n. the death of a person, or the sorrow felt because of it
(4) n. money that a person or business loses, i.e. spending more than is earned

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (比赛、竞选的)失利、败北
uncommonMeanings.example: The narrow loss in the final robbed them of the trophy, yet the way the young players held their heads high won the crowd's deepest respect. （读后续写·体育·虽败犹荣）

posExamples.sentence: Standing at her grandmother's graveside, Lucy felt the loss settle over her like a heavy fog, and for the first time she understood that some absences never truly fade. （读后续写·亲情·丧亲之痛）
On behalf of the whole club, I am writing to express our deep sorrow at the loss of our beloved coach, whose warmth and wisdom shaped a generation of players. （应用文·慰问信）
The loss of biodiversity is not merely an environmental concern; it is a warning that the delicate web sustaining all life is beginning to unravel. （议论文·环境保护）
Despite months of hard work, the small café ran at a loss all winter, and by spring the owner faced the painful decision of closing its doors. （读后续写·创业·困境）

idioms.example: Realising the venture was doomed, the wise old merchant advised his son to cut his losses and start afresh elsewhere. （读后续写·经商·智慧）

idioms.translation: 毫无用处的人/物；全然的损失
idioms.example: Everyone had written the stubborn old bicycle off as a dead loss, but Grandpa restored it, gear by rusty gear, into a gleaming machine. （读后续写·祖孙·匠心）

collocations.example: When the interviewer suddenly switched to fluent French, the nervous candidate was momentarily at a loss. （读后续写·面试·窘迫）
The loss of her eyesight did not dim Helen's spirit; instead, she learned to see the world through the fingertips of her heart. （读后续写·励志·身残志坚）
The flood-stricken village suffered a heavy loss, yet neighbours from across the province rushed in with food, tents and hope. （读后续写·灾难·守望相助）

collocations.phrase: make a loss / run at a loss
collocations.example: Rather than raise prices during the shortage, the honest grocer chose to run at a loss so that no family in the town would go hungry. （读后续写·善良·坚守）
When her closest friend moved abroad, a quiet sense of loss followed Emma into every familiar corner of the empty classroom. （读后续写·友情·离别）

collocations.phrase: weight loss / memory loss / job loss
collocations.translation: 体重下降/记忆丧失/失业
collocations.example: The sudden job loss shook him to the core, but it also freed him to chase the dream he had buried for twenty years. （读后续写·转折·重生）
One harsh remark from the judge triggered a loss of confidence that took the young violinist months to overcome. （读后续写·成长·挫折）
Weighing the profit and loss coolly, the manager concluded that long-term trust mattered far more than short-term gain. （议论文·商业道德）

synonyms.example: The bitter defeat taught the team a lesson no victory ever could. （读后续写·体育·成长）
synonyms.usage: 特指竞赛、战斗、竞选中"被击败"，含对抗色彩；loss 更泛，可指失去、去世、亏损等各种"失"

synonyms.example: The storm caused severe damage to the coastal town's fishing fleet. （应用文·新闻报道）
synonyms.usage: 强调对物体或事物造成的"破坏、损伤"，多为物质层面；loss 强调"失去、缺少"这一结果本身

synonyms.example: Sleep deprivation gradually eroded her focus, and the once-brilliant student began to fall behind. （议论文·健康）
synonyms.usage: 书面、正式，强调"被剥夺"重要事物，含被动与匮乏意味；loss 更中性通用

advancedExpressions.expression: out of loss came ...
advancedExpressions.example: Out of loss came an unexpected gift: a tenderness towards every fleeting moment she had once taken for granted. （倒装 + 抽象化，将"失去"转化为成长感悟，续写升华段）

advancedExpressions.expression: words can hardly express our sorrow at the loss of ...

advancedExpressions.expression: the true loss lies not in ... but in ...
advancedExpressions.example: The true loss lies not in the failure itself but in the courage we surrender the moment we stop trying. （对比结构重新定义"损失"，深化论点）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She was very sad about the loss of her dog.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The loss of her old collie left a silence in the house so profound that even the ticking of the clock seemed to mourn, and Grace found herself listening, night after night, for a bark that would never come again. （读后续写·失去宠物·哀伤）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 拟人(the clock seemed to mourn) + 环境烘托(silence) + 细节想象(bark that would never come) 强化悲伤

sentenceUpgrade.original: The loss of forests is a big problem.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The relentless loss of forests, far from being a distant concern, strikes at the very foundation on which our shared future is built, silencing countless species and stealing the breath from generations yet unborn. （议论文·环境）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: far from being 插入让步 + strike at the foundation 隐喻 + 现在分词并列(silencing... stealing...)递进升华

original_sentence: The stress of this situation is killing me, and I'm at a loss what to do next.
readingExamples: The stress of this situation is killing me, and I'm at a loss what to do next.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. so confused or uncertain that you do not know what to do or say
(2) phr. (at a loss for words) unable to think of anything to say, especially because of surprise or strong emotion
(3) phr. (of a business) making less money than is spent; not making a profit

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (做生意)亏本地，赔钱地
uncommonMeanings.example: Rather than dump the surplus, the kind-hearted farmer sold his apples at a loss so that the orphanage could taste fresh fruit that autumn. （读后续写·善良·奉献）

posExamples.sentence: When the examiner asked a question she had never anticipated, Mia stood there utterly at a loss, her carefully rehearsed answers scattering like leaves in the wind. （读后续写·面试·慌乱）
If you ever find yourself at a loss about how to settle a quarrel with a friend, please do not hesitate to drop by our student counselling centre. （应用文·倡议/建议信）
Confronted with the sheer scale of the crisis, even seasoned experts confessed they were at a loss, a reminder that humility must accompany all human knowledge. （议论文·科技与人性）
So overwhelmed was she by the surprise party that, for a long moment, this normally eloquent girl was completely at a loss for words. （读后续写·惊喜·感动）

idioms.translation: 一时语塞，不知说什么好
idioms.example: When the shy boy handed her the flowers he had grown himself, the teacher was so moved that she was at a loss for words. （读后续写·师生·温情）

collocations.phrase: be at a loss what to do
collocations.example: Stranded at the deserted station past midnight, the young traveller was at a loss what to do until a kindly guard offered him shelter. （读后续写·陌生人善意）

collocations.phrase: be at a loss to explain / understand
collocations.example: Scientists were at a loss to explain why the migrating birds had suddenly changed their thousand-year-old route. （议论文·自然之谜）

collocations.phrase: be at a loss for words
collocations.example: Reading her late mother's final letter, she was at a loss for words, the ink blurring beneath her falling tears. （读后续写·亲情·遗物）
Newly arrived in the bustling city, the country boy often found himself at a loss amid the maze of neon signs and hurrying strangers. （读后续写·进城·迷茫）
Determined to keep his loyal workers employed, the owner sold his stock at a loss throughout the harsh winter. （读后续写·企业·担当）

synonyms.example: The confused tourist turned the map upside down, only to grow more bewildered than before. （读后续写·旅途·迷路）
synonyms.usage: 普通形容词，泛指"思维混乱、弄不明白"；at a loss 是短语，更强调"茫然到不知如何行动或开口"

synonyms.translation: 迷惑不解的，不知所措的
synonyms.example: Bewildered by the sudden applause, the modest volunteer had no idea her small act had touched so many. （读后续写·意外·感动）
synonyms.usage: 书面且情绪更强，突出被复杂情形"弄糊涂"；at a loss 侧重"无计可施、无言以对"的状态

synonyms.example: Watching the flood swallow her family's field, the little girl felt utterly helpless. （读后续写·灾难·无力）
synonyms.usage: 强调"无力改变、得不到帮助"；at a loss 更偏"一时想不出办法"的心理空白

advancedExpressions.expression: at a loss, sb. could only ...
advancedExpressions.example: At a loss, she could only stand frozen at the threshold, her heart pounding against a silence that seemed to swallow every word. （用短语前置 + could only 刻画茫然瞬间的定格感）

advancedExpressions.expression: whenever you are at a loss, remember that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Whenever you are at a loss about your future, remember that even the longest journey begins with a single, trembling step. （建议信中给出鼓励，句式温暖有力）

advancedExpressions.expression: being at a loss is not weakness but ...
advancedExpressions.example: Being at a loss, far from a sign of weakness, is often the honest starting point from which genuine wisdom begins to grow. （重新定义"茫然"，赋予其积极意义）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He didn't know what to do.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: For a heartbeat he stood at a loss, the shouts of the crowd fading into a distant hum, his mind a blank page on which no plan would write itself. （读后续写·危急时刻·心理留白）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: at a loss 替换 didn't know + 环境虚化(fading into a hum) + 比喻(blank page)呈现思维空白

sentenceUpgrade.original: Many young people are at a loss about their careers.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: That so many young people today find themselves at a loss about their careers is less a personal failing than a reflection of an age drowning in choices yet starved of direction. （议论文·青年成长）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: That 从句作主语 + less...than 对比重估归因 + 反义并列(drowning in choices yet starved of direction)升华

translation: 评价，(尤指)批评；判断，认为 | n. 法官；裁判员
original_sentence: Don't be so quick to judge your friend.
readingExamples: Don't be so quick to judge your friend.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. & vi. to form or give an opinion about someone or something after careful thought
(2) vt. & vi. to decide the result of a competition, or to act as a referee
(3) vt. to criticize someone, especially in an unfair or hasty way
(4) n. an official who makes decisions in a court of law
(5) n. a person who decides the winner in a competition, or who can give a valued opinion

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 行家，鉴赏家(a good judge of sth)
uncommonMeanings.example: Grandfather was a shrewd judge of character, and one glance at the smiling stranger was enough to make him tighten his grip on my hand. （读后续写·长辈·识人）

posExamples.sentence: Don't judge the timid new boy too harshly, Amy told herself; behind his silence might lie a story far heavier than her own. （读后续写·校园·包容）
I am honoured to invite you to judge our annual English speech contest, as your rich experience would lend great authority to the event. （应用文·邀请信）
We should never judge a person's worth by the clothes they wear or the accent they speak with, for true character lies far beneath the surface. （议论文·平等与偏见）
As the final note faded, the head judge rose to her feet, and the thunderous applause told everyone the verdict before she spoke a word. （读后续写·比赛·高潮）

idioms.idiom: don't judge a book by its cover
idioms.example: Ragged and mud-stained, the old man was ignored by everyone until he sat down and played the piano like a master — truly, one should never judge a book by its cover. （读后续写·反转·偏见）
Judging by the dark clouds massing over the mountains, we quickened our pace toward the shelter. （读后续写·徒步·天气）

idioms.idiom: as far as I can judge
idioms.example: As far as I can judge, the plan is both practical and fair, and I sincerely hope the committee will approve it. （应用文·建议信）

collocations.example: You cannot judge a student's ability by a single test, for a bad day says nothing about a bright future. （议论文·教育评价）
Rather than take my word for it, come to the exhibition and judge for yourself the astonishing talent of these young painters. （应用文·倡议信）
"Don't be so quick to judge her," Cindy urged gently; "perhaps there is more to the story than you know." （读后续写·友情·劝解）

collocations.phrase: a good / poor judge of sth
collocations.example: Years of coaching had made him an excellent judge of raw talent, and he spotted the champion in her at once. （读后续写·伯乐·慧眼）
Three renowned chefs were invited to judge the school cooking contest, tasting each dish with painstaking care. （应用文·活动报道）
The captain judged that the storm would pass by dawn, so he ordered the crew to hold their course. （读后续写·航海·决断）
Quickly judging the distance to the far bank, the boy took a deep breath and leapt. （读后续写·冒险·瞬间抉择）
Judging by appearances alone, no one would have guessed that the shy cleaner had once been a celebrated scholar. （读后续写·反差·尊重）

synonyms.example: The teacher carefully assessed each project not just for its result but for the effort behind it. （议论文·教育公平）
synonyms.usage: 正式、中性，强调依据标准"衡量、估价"，多用于能力、价值、风险；judge 更口语，也含"评断、批评"意味

synonyms.example: It is far easier to criticize others than to examine our own faults with the same honesty. （议论文·自省）
synonyms.usage: 特指"挑毛病、指责"，含明显负面色彩；judge 表"批评"义时多指仓促、片面的评断，语气略缓

synonyms.example: Before we condemn a new policy, we ought to evaluate its long-term effects with a cool head. （议论文·理性思考）
synonyms.usage: 书面且系统，强调"综合分析后作出评价"；judge 可以是瞬间、直觉的判断，也可指法律裁决

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. learned never to judge ... by ...
advancedExpressions.example: That day Amy learned never to judge a friend by a single careless act, for one moment can never sum up an entire heart. （用"学会不轻易评判"点出成长主题，续写主旨句）

advancedExpressions.expression: we would be greatly honoured if you could judge ...
advancedExpressions.example: We would be greatly honoured if you could judge our charity art show, as your discerning eye would mean the world to these young artists. （邀请信正式而恳切）

advancedExpressions.expression: before we rush to judge, we ought to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Before we rush to judge others for their choices, we ought to walk, if only for a moment, in the shoes they have worn. （"评判前先换位"，呼吁包容，句式含条件插入语）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Don't judge people too quickly.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Before you let a single glance harden into judgement, pause and remember that every face you pass conceals a battle you know nothing about. （读后续写/议论文·换位思考）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Before you...祈使前置 + 抽象名词化(a glance harden into judgement) + conceals a battle 隐喻唤起共情

sentenceUpgrade.original: The judges chose her as the winner.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: When the judges, after a long and thoughtful silence, finally declared her the winner, the trembling girl who had once been laughed at now stood bathed in a light she had only dared to dream of. （读后续写·逆袭·高光时刻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: after a long silence 插入营造悬念 + 定语从句回溯过往(once been laughed at) + bathed in a light 光影隐喻升华

original_sentence: Perhaps she knows she's in the wrong and wants to apologize, or maybe she has a simple explanation for her behaviour.
readingExamples: Perhaps she knows she's in the wrong and wants to apologize, or maybe she has a simple explanation for her behaviour.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. responsible for a mistake, an accident, or a quarrel; being the one who has done something bad or incorrect
(2) phr. mistaken in one's actions or judgement; at fault (opposite of 'in the right')

posExamples.sentence: Halfway through her furious speech, Amy suddenly realised she was in the wrong, and the words died in her throat as shame crept up her cheeks. （读后续写·争吵·悔悟）
If, after reading this letter, you still feel our club is in the wrong, we sincerely apologize and promise to make things right at once. （应用文·道歉信）
A truly big-hearted person is willing to admit being in the wrong, for humility, not stubbornness, is the mark of real strength. （议论文·品格）
Perhaps she knew she was in the wrong and longed to say sorry, yet pride kept sealing her lips each time she reached for the phone. （读后续写·矛盾·心理挣扎）

idioms.translation: (使)显得某人有错，把责任推给某人
idioms.example: By twisting my innocent remark, he cleverly put me in the wrong before the whole class. （读后续写·校园·委屈）

collocations.example: The moment he saw the tears in his mother's eyes, the boy knew he had been in the wrong all along. （读后续写·亲情·内疚）

collocations.phrase: admit (that) one is in the wrong
collocations.example: It takes real courage to admit you are in the wrong and greater courage still to make amends. （议论文·勇气与担当）

collocations.phrase: know / feel one is in the wrong
collocations.example: Deep down she felt she was in the wrong, and that quiet guilt gnawed at her all through the sleepless night. （读后续写·悔恨·失眠）
In any dispute, the party in the wrong should have the grace to take the first step towards reconciliation. （议论文·和解）

collocations.phrase: prove sb (to be) in the wrong
collocations.example: The security footage clearly proved the reckless driver to be in the wrong. （应用文·事件报道）

synonyms.example: When the vase shattered, everyone assumed the cat was at fault, but the real culprit was the gust from the open window. （读后续写·误会·真相）
synonyms.usage: 与 in the wrong 近乎同义，都指"负有责任、有过错"；at fault 稍中性，常用于事故、失误的归责，语气略客观

synonyms.example: No single person was entirely to blame for the misunderstanding; both had spoken in anger. （读后续写·矛盾·反思）
synonyms.usage: 强调"该受责怪、担责"，常与 be 连用(be to blame)；in the wrong 更侧重"处于错误、理亏的一方"这一状态

synonyms.example: I was mistaken about her intentions, and I have regretted my hasty words ever since. （读后续写·误解·愧疚）
synonyms.usage: 指"判断、看法有误"，偏认知层面，未必涉及道德过错；in the wrong 常含"理亏、该道歉"的责任意味

advancedExpressions.expression: only when ... did sb. realise sb. had been in the wrong
advancedExpressions.example: Only when she saw the letter, unsent and tear-stained, did Amy realise how badly she had been in the wrong. （倒装 + 细节实证(tear-stained letter)，续写悔悟段的高光句）

advancedExpressions.expression: on reflection, I admit that we were in the wrong, and ...

advancedExpressions.expression: admitting one is in the wrong is not a defeat but ...
advancedExpressions.example: Admitting that one is in the wrong is not a defeat but a quiet triumph of conscience over pride. （否定+对比结构，重估"认错"的价值）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She knew she was wrong and wanted to apologize.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Somewhere beneath her stubborn silence, Amy knew she was in the wrong, and a small, insistent voice kept urging her to pick up the phone and simply say sorry before it was too late. （读后续写·心理挣扎）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 环境化心理(beneath her stubborn silence) + in the wrong 替换 wrong + 拟人(a small insistent voice) + before it was too late 制造紧迫

sentenceUpgrade.original: The person who is in the wrong should apologize first.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is the one who is truly in the wrong, rather than the one who shouts the loudest, who ought to have the humility to apologize first and mend what anger has broken. （议论文·和解与担当）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is...who 强调句 + rather than 对比(错的人 vs 嗓门大的人) + 定语从句 + mend what anger has broken 隐喻收尾

original_sentence: Perhaps she knows she's in the wrong and wants to apologize, or maybe she has a simple explanation for her behaviour.
readingExamples: Perhaps she knows she's in the wrong and wants to apologize, or maybe she has a simple explanation for her behaviour.
definitionEn:
(1) vi. to tell someone that you are sorry for having done something that has caused them harm, trouble, or inconvenience
(2) vi. to make a formal statement of regret, especially in speech or writing (also spelled 'apologise' in British English)

posExamples.sentence: Swallowing her pride, Amy walked up to her friend and apologized in a trembling voice, and to her surprise, all it took was two small words to melt a week of frost between them. （读后续写·和解·释怀）
I am writing to apologize sincerely for missing the group meeting last Friday, as a sudden family emergency left me no chance to inform you in advance. （应用文·道歉信）
A society that teaches its children to apologize when they err is nurturing not weakness, but the moral courage on which trust and harmony depend. （议论文·品德教育）
"I should never have shouted at you," the old man apologized, his weathered hands shaking as he reached out to the grandson he had wronged. （读后续写·祖孙·愧疚）

collocations.example: She finally apologized to her mother for the harsh words that had hung between them for weeks. （读后续写·亲情·和好）
The waiter apologized profusely and replaced the spilt soup with a warm smile that dissolved my irritation at once. （读后续写·陌生人·温暖）
Rather than send a quick text, he chose to apologize in person, walking two miles through the rain to reach her door. （读后续写·真诚·担当）

collocations.translation: 欠某人一个道歉(名词形式高频搭配)
collocations.example: Deep down, Tom knew he owed his little sister an apology, yet the words seemed to stick stubbornly in his throat. （读后续写·手足·内疚）
The company publicly apologized for causing the delay and promised to compensate every affected customer. （应用文·公告）
A heartfelt apology, offered without excuses, can heal wounds that time alone would leave open. （议论文·人际关系）
With a gentle smile she accepted his apology, and the long shadow of their quarrel finally lifted. （读后续写·宽恕·释然）

synonyms.example: Sometimes the hardest thing in the world is to look someone in the eye and simply say sorry. （读后续写·成长·勇气）
synonyms.usage: 最口语、直白，多用于日常和对话；apologize 更正式，适用于书面、公开或郑重场合

synonyms.example: The headmaster expressed deep regret over the incident and pledged that such carelessness would never happen again. （应用文·正式声明）
synonyms.usage: 书面且正式，突出"表达遗憾、抱歉之情"，语气庄重；apologize 更直接明确地承认过错并致歉

synonyms.example: Words were not enough, so he spent the whole weekend rebuilding the fence to make amends for his carelessness. （读后续写·行动·补过）
synonyms.usage: 强调"用行动补救"，重在弥补而非言语；apologize 侧重"用言语致歉"，二者常前后呼应

advancedExpressions.expression: no sooner had sb. apologized than ...
advancedExpressions.example: No sooner had she apologized than the tears she had held back all week finally broke free, and the two friends fell into a long, forgiving embrace. （倒装 no sooner...than + 情感爆发，续写高潮和解段）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I was sure I could win.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As I stared down the empty track, one thought burned definitely bright in my mind, silencing every whisper of doubt: this race, at long last, was going to be mine. （读后续写·赛前决心）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 环境铺垫(stared down the track) + definitely 强化确信 + 冒号引出内心宣言 + 拟人(whisper of doubt)

sentenceUpgrade.original: Honesty is very important.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Honesty, I would argue, is definitely the foundation on which all lasting trust is built — for once a lie cracks that foundation, no amount of charm can ever make it whole again. （议论文·诚实的根基）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: I would argue 插入语 + definitely 加强断言 + 隐喻(foundation) + for引导因果+ 强化对比(cracks vs whole)

translation: 欺骗，欺诈 | n. 诡计，花招；戏法
original_sentence: When I found out that I was tricked by him, I was really hurt and let go of our friendship.
readingExamples: When I found out that I was tricked by him, I was really hurt and let go of our friendship.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to deceive someone in order to get something from them or to make them do something
(2) n. something you do to deceive someone or to make someone believe something that is not true
(3) n. a clever or skilful action or scheme that achieves a particular result, especially an unexpected one
(4) n. an act of skill performed to entertain, such as a magic trick or an acrobatic feat

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 诀窍，窍门(常作 the trick)
uncommonMeanings.example: The old carpenter smiled and showed the boy the trick of it: not brute force, but a patient wrist and a listening ear for the grain of the wood. （读后续写·师徒传艺·诀窍）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (牌戏中)一圈牌，一墩
uncommonMeanings.example: With the very last card she won the final trick, and the quiet triumph in her grandfather's eyes was worth more to her than the game itself. （读后续写·亲情·打牌）

posExamples.sentence: When I realised the smooth-talking salesman had tricked my grandmother into buying a useless machine, a hot wave of anger rose in me, and I vowed to get her money back. （读后续写·维护家人）
I am writing to warn all fellow students of a common online trick in which fraudsters pose as teachers to steal login details and personal information. （应用文·警示通知）
There is no magic trick to mastering a language; steady, daily effort, however dull it may seem, is the only reliable road to fluency. （议论文·学习）
The street performer's final trick left the crowd gasping, for the coin that had vanished from his empty palm reappeared, impossibly, behind a child's ear. （读后续写·街头表演）

wordForms.noun: trick, trickery (n. 欺骗，骗术), trickster (n. 骗子)
wordForms.adjective: tricky (adj. 棘手的；狡猾的), trickish

idioms.idiom: play a trick / tricks on sb
idioms.example: His classmates loved to play tricks on the new boy, until the day he laughed hardest of all and, just like that, became one of them. （读后续写·融入集体）
A cup of hot ginger tea and an early night usually did the trick whenever a cold threatened to ruin her exams. （读后续写·生活智慧）

idioms.translation: 行业诀窍，做某事的窍门
idioms.example: Over thirty years at the market stall, the old woman had learned every one of the tricks of the trade, and she passed them on to her granddaughter one patient morning at a time. （读后续写·传承）
The coach tried every trick in the book to lift the exhausted team's spirits before the final quarter. （读后续写·激励）
Spreading that rumour was a dirty trick, and it left a stain on their friendship that no apology could fully wash away. （读后续写·背叛）

collocations.example: The con man tricked the villagers into handing over their savings, but justice, though slow, finally caught up with him. （读后续写·善恶有报）
She could hardly believe that a stranger's smile had tricked her out of a month's wages in a single afternoon. （读后续写·受骗）
The birthday party lit up the moment the magician pulled off a magic trick that turned an empty hat into a fluttering white dove. （读后续写·节日）
Winning an argument with a cheap trick may feel clever for a moment, but it costs you the one thing worth having — respect. （议论文·辩论道德）
She discovered a clever trick for remembering long lists: turning each item into a vivid picture in an imaginary house. （应用文·学习分享）

collocations.translation: 陷阱问题，故意误导人的问题
collocations.example: The teacher's trick question caught out everyone who had memorised the rules without ever pausing to understand them. （议论文·死记硬背）
His only party trick was balancing a spoon on his nose, yet somehow it never failed to break the ice with strangers. （读后续写·社交）
Do not underestimate the quiet old gardener — after fifty springs among these roses, he knows a trick or two that no book can teach. （读后续写·人物）

synonyms.example: He had deceived everyone around him for years, but the one person he could never deceive, in the end, was himself. （读后续写·良心）
synonyms.usage: 较正式，泛指‘用谎言使人相信假象’；trick(v.)更口语，强调‘用花招骗人做某事或骗取某物’，常接 into / out of

synonyms.example: You may fool some people for a while, but a lie, like smoke, always finds its way out into the open at last. （议论文·诚实）
synonyms.usage: 口语，强调‘使人上当、显得愚蠢’；与 trick 意思相近，但 trick 更突出‘用计谋、有具体手段’

synonyms.example: Rather than cheat his way to an easy victory, he chose the harder road of honest effort and slept soundly for it. （议论文·诚信）
synonyms.usage: 侧重‘为私利而违反规则或坑骗他人(尤指钱财、考试)’；trick 更侧重‘用巧计诱使’，不一定涉及规则

advancedExpressions.expression: the moment I realised I had been tricked, ...
advancedExpressions.example: The moment I realised I had been tricked, the warm glow of the afternoon curdled into cold fury, and I set off after him with a determination I did not know I possessed. （用被动 be tricked 引爆情绪转折）

advancedExpressions.expression: do not be tricked by ...; always ...
advancedExpressions.example: Do not be tricked by messages promising easy money or free prizes; always verify the sender and, when in doubt, tell a trusted adult at once. （警示信中给出具体建议）

advancedExpressions.expression: there is no trick, no shortcut — only ...
advancedExpressions.example: When it comes to earning genuine respect, there is no trick, no shortcut, no clever scheme — only the slow, honest accumulation of deeds that speak for themselves. （否定排比，强调无捷径）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I found out he had tricked me and felt hurt.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: When at last I pieced the truth together and understood that the friend I had trusted most had tricked me all along, something inside me quietly broke — and in the silence that followed, I let go of the friendship I had once believed unbreakable. （读后续写·失望与放手）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 时间状语层层推进(When at last...) + trick 的被动过去完成时 + quietly broke 心理描写 + 破折号+对比(unbreakable) 收尾

sentenceUpgrade.original: There is no easy way to succeed.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Let us be honest: there is no magic trick to success, no secret shortcut hidden from the crowd — only the unglamorous, day-after-day discipline that the impatient are never willing to pay. （议论文·成功无捷径）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Let us be honest 呼告 + no...no...only 否定排比 + magic trick / shortcut 具象化 + 破折号强调核心观点

original_sentence: When I found out that I was tricked by him, I was really hurt and let go of our friendship.
readingExamples: When I found out that I was tricked by him, I was really hurt and let go of our friendship.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. v. to stop holding something or someone with your hands
(2) phr. v. to stop trying to keep, control, or possess something
(3) phr. v. to accept that a relationship, feeling, or period of your life is over and move on emotionally
(4) phr. v. to give up or abandon (an idea, grievance, or attachment)

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 解雇，辞退（=let sb. go）
uncommonMeanings.example: When the factory finally had to let go of a third of its workforce, the old foreman shook each man's hand at the gate, unable to meet their eyes. （读后续写·经济困境·人物尊严）

posExamples.sentence: Her fingers, white with strain, refused to let go of the rope, even as her arms trembled and the cliff edge crumbled beneath her feet — she would not fall, not today. （读后续写·危机时刻·动作描写）
I have come to realise that in order to grow, we must sometimes let go of the resentment we cling to, for it poisons the one who carries it far more than the one who caused it. （应用文·感悊信/回信）
Those who cannot let go of past failures are doomed to be imprisoned by them; genuine progress begins only when we release our grip on what we can no longer change. （议论文·成长与释怀）
As the balloon slipped from the little girl's hand and drifted skyward, she did not cry; instead she waved, having chosen to let go of it with a smile rather than a scream. （读后续写·童年·情感成长）

idioms.example: Standing before his father's grave, he finally let go of the past — the years of silence, the words unsaid — and whispered a long-overdue goodbye. （读后续写·和解·情感升华）

collocations.phrase: let go of the rope / handle / rail
collocations.example: "Don't let go of the rail!" the guide shouted over the roar of the waterfall, but by then it was too late. （读后续写·探险·紧张场面）
Reluctantly, the mother let go of her son's small hand at the school gate, watching him disappear into a new chapter of his life. （读后续写·亲情·离别）

collocations.phrase: let go of a dream / an idea
collocations.example: Despite years of rejection, she refused to let go of her dream of becoming a novelist, and one grey morning a publisher's letter finally proved her right. （读后续写·励志·坚持）

collocations.phrase: let go of anger / resentment / grudges
collocations.example: Learning to let go of anger is not a sign of weakness but of remarkable inner strength. （议论文·情绪管理）
The moment she let go of the fear that had held her back for years, her voice rang out clear and steady across the silent auditorium. （读后续写·演讲·突破自我）
Good parents must learn to let go, allowing their children the freedom to stumble, fail, and ultimately find their own path. （应用文·家庭教育·观点）
A truly effective leader knows when to let go of control and trust the team to rise to the occasion. （议论文·领导力）

collocations.phrase: find it hard to let go of
collocations.example: Even after decades abroad, he found it hard to let go of the accent, the recipes, and the small rituals of his hometown. （读后续写·乡愁）

synonyms.example: With a deep breath, she released the tension in her shoulders and the grip on her worn suitcase, ready at last to begin again. （读后续写·释然）
synonyms.usage: 较正式、书面；既可指松开物体，也可指释放情绪，续写中比 let go of 更凝练

synonyms.example: He was tempted to give up halfway through the marathon, but the cheers of the crowd carried him across the finish line. （读后续写·坚持）
synonyms.usage: 侧重停止努力或戒除，含消极意味；let go of 更强调情感上的释怀与放手，不必然消极

synonyms.example: The retiring chairman gracefully relinquished his authority, confident that a new generation would carry the company forward. （议论文·交接与传承）
synonyms.usage: 非常正式，多指放弃权力、地位、权利；议论文/正式文体用之显得高级

advancedExpressions.expression: only by letting go of ... could sb. finally ...
advancedExpressions.example: Only by letting go of the guilt she had carried for so long could she finally look at her reflection and forgive the girl staring back. （倒装+抽象名词具象化，续写结尾释怀升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: I would gently encourage you to let go of ..., for ...
advancedExpressions.example: I would gently encourage you to let go of the blame you place upon yourself, for the accident was never within your power to prevent. （劝慰信，语气温和+原因状语从句）

advancedExpressions.expression: to let go of ... is not to ..., but to ...
advancedExpressions.example: To let go of a cherished plan is not to admit defeat, but to make room for a wiser and worthier path. （否定对比结构，辨证论证，升华主旨）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She let go of the rope.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: For one endless heartbeat she clung on; then, drawing a shuddering breath, she let go of the rope and surrendered herself to the churning water below — trusting, for the first time in her life, that she would surface. （读后续写·抉择+心理描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: for one endless heartbeat 时间凝滞 + 分词状语(drawing a shuddering breath)描写细节 + 破折号补充心理 + surrender/surface 押头韵

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should let go of the past.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is my firm belief that only when we summon the courage to let go of past grievances can we free ourselves from their invisible chains and stride, unburdened, towards the future. （议论文·观点论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is my firm belief that 正式主句 + only when 引导倒装强调 + invisible chains 比喻 + unburdened 插入语+ stride 动词升级

original_sentence: However, if your friend ignores your feelings or makes you suffer, it's time to rethink your relationship.
readingExamples: However, if your friend ignores your feelings or makes you suffer, it's time to rethink your relationship.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to deliberately pay no attention to someone or something
(2) vt. to behave as if you have not heard or noticed someone or something
(3) vt. to fail to consider something important when making a decision or judgement
(4) vt. to take no notice of a rule, warning, or fact

posExamples.sentence: She swept past him in the corridor, chin held high, choosing to ignore the outstretched hand and the apology trembling on his lips — pride, she would later learn, is a lonely companion. （读后续写·冷战·人物心理）
I sincerely hope that you will not ignore the safety instructions posted at the entrance, as they are designed to protect every visitor during the exhibition. （应用文·通知/须知）
To ignore the warnings of scientists on climate change is not merely unwise; it is a reckless gamble with the future of generations yet unborn. （议论文·环境·论证）
For weeks the boy had ignored the stray dog shivering by the gate, but one snowy evening his conscience would let him ignore it no longer. （读后续写·善良·转折）

collocations.example: A true friend will never ignore your feelings, no matter how busy life becomes. （应用文·友谊·观点）
Had he not ignored his coach's advice about pacing, he might have finished the race on his feet rather than in an ambulance. （读后续写·教训）
We cannot ignore the fact that excessive screen time is quietly eroding the concentration of our young people. （议论文·科技·论证）
Those who habitually ignore the rules of the road put not only themselves but also countless strangers at risk. （议论文·公共安全）
He deliberately ignored her calls for three whole days, and the silence widened between them like a river no bridge could span. （读后续写·关系疏远·比喻）
Ignoring the problem will not make it disappear; it will only allow it to fester until it becomes impossible to solve. （议论文·问题应对）
The role of mental health in academic success is far too important to ignore. （应用文·倡议·呼吁）
The new student sat alone at lunch, ignored entirely by the noisy circles around her, until one quiet girl slid a tray across the table. （读后续写·善意·校园）

synonyms.example: In his obsession with success, he had neglected the very people who loved him most. （读后续写·反思·亲情）
synonyms.usage: 侧重因疏忽或未尽责而忽略，含责备意味；ignore 是主动、故意地不理会

synonyms.example: In our rush to praise the winners, we often overlook the quiet perseverance of those who never made the podium. （议论文·公平）
synonyms.usage: 多指无意中看漏、没注意到；ignore 更强调明知却故意不理

synonyms.example: The committee chose to disregard the objections and pushed the controversial plan through. （议论文·决策）
synonyms.usage: 正式书面语，语气比 ignore 更强，常指无视规则、意见、事实

synonyms.example: Teachers who turn a blind eye to bullying unwittingly become accomplices to it. （议论文·校园·论证）
synonyms.usage: 习语，强调明知有错却故意装作没看见，带道德批评色彩

advancedExpressions.expression: try as sb. might to ignore ..., ...
advancedExpressions.example: Try as she might to ignore the ticking of the clock, each second seemed to hammer against her racing heart. （倒装让步状语+拟物，营造紧张感）

advancedExpressions.expression: we can no longer afford to ignore ...
advancedExpressions.example: As members of this community, we can no longer afford to ignore the mountains of waste piling up behind our school. （倡议书，呼吁行动，afford 表"承担得起"）

advancedExpressions.expression: to ignore ... is to invite ...
advancedExpressions.example: To ignore the lessons of history is to invite the repetition of its darkest chapters. （不定式主语对称结构，警示式论断）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He ignored her.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: He walked straight past her as though she were made of glass — transparent, weightless, unworthy of even a flicker of recognition — and something inside her quietly broke. （读后续写·冷落+心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: as though 虚拟比喻(made of glass) + 三个形容词递进(transparent, weightless, unworthy) + 破折号插入 + quietly broke 抽象情感具象化

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not ignore this problem.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It would be nothing short of irresponsible to turn a blind eye to a problem that, if left unaddressed, threatens to undermine the very foundation of our society. （议论文·论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It would be nothing short of + 形容词 强调 + turn a blind eye to 习语替换 + if left unaddressed 省略状语从句 + the very foundation 强调

translation: 受苦，受折磨；变差 | vt. 遭受，蒙受
original_sentence: However, if your friend ignores your feelings or makes you suffer, it's time to rethink your relationship.
readingExamples: However, if your friend ignores your feelings or makes you suffer, it's time to rethink your relationship.
definitionEn:
(1) vi. to experience physical or mental pain, distress, or hardship
(2) vt. to experience or be subjected to something unpleasant (an injury, loss, defeat, etc.)
(3) vi. to become worse in quality or performance; to be badly affected
(4) vi. suffer from — to have a particular illness, problem, or condition over a period of time

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （古／正式）容忍，忍受（=tolerate）
uncommonMeanings.example: "Suffer the little children to come unto me," the old preacher read, and for a moment the restless village fell utterly still. （读后续写·乡村教堂·庄重氛围）

posExamples.sentence: Night after night the widow suffered in silence, her tears soaking the pillow long after the house had fallen dark, yet each dawn she rose and smiled for her children. （读后续写·坚韧·母爱）
I am writing to inform you that our football team suffered a narrow defeat in the final, yet the players' spirit never wavered throughout the match. （应用文·报道/来信）
When students are deprived of adequate sleep, both their health and their academic performance inevitably suffer. （议论文·作息·因果论证）
Grandpa suffered from a weak heart, yet he insisted on climbing the hill each morning to watch the sun spill gold over the valley he had farmed all his life. （读后续写·祖辈·热爱生活）

idioms.example: Rather than suffer in silence, she finally found the courage to speak up about the injustice she had endured. （读后续写·觉醒·维权）
The old professor was brilliant but did not suffer fools gladly, dismissing lazy answers with a single raised eyebrow. （读后续写·人物刻画）

collocations.example: Millions of teenagers today suffer from anxiety, a silent epidemic that deserves far more attention than it receives. （议论文·心理健康）
Having suffered one setback after another, the young inventor refused to abandon the design that would one day change lives. （读后续写·励志·坚持）
Several passengers suffered minor injuries when the bus skidded on the icy road, but the quick-thinking driver prevented a far greater tragedy. （应用文·新闻报道）
Those who cheat their way to success will sooner or later suffer the consequences of their dishonesty. （议论文·诚信）
No child should be left to suffer in silence; a single caring adult can change everything. （应用文·关爱倡议）
His careless words made her suffer far more than he could ever imagine. （读后续写·伤害·后悔）
The refugees had suffered greatly on their long journey, yet gratitude, not bitterness, shone in their weary eyes. （读后续写·苦难·人性光辉）
When a company chases profit at the expense of its workers, the quality of its products inevitably suffers. （议论文·商业伦理）

synonyms.example: For three long winters the explorers endured hunger and biting cold, sustained only by the dream of reaching the pole. （读后续写·探险·坚韧）
synonyms.usage: 强调有意志地坚持忍受，含褒义的坚韧色彩；suffer 更侧重被动地承受痛苦

synonyms.example: The patient bravely underwent a series of painful treatments, buoyed by the unwavering support of his family. （读后续写·病痛·亲情）
synonyms.usage: 中性词，指经历（尤指困难或变化的过程），不必然含痛苦；suffer 明确带痛苦义

synonyms.example: She bore the weight of the family's expectations with a quiet dignity that moved everyone who knew her. （读后续写·责任·尊严）
synonyms.usage: 指承担、忍受重负或痛苦，常搭配 pain/burden；suffer 更强调痛苦的体验本身

advancedExpressions.expression: having suffered so much, sb. had learned that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Having suffered so much, she had learned that scars are not marks of shame but silent testaments to survival. （分词状语+格言式升华，续写结尾）

advancedExpressions.expression: no one should have to suffer ... alone
advancedExpressions.example: No one should have to suffer the burden of illness alone, which is precisely why our volunteer team exists. （倡议书，which 引导非限定强调宗旨）

advancedExpressions.expression: when ..., it is invariably ... that suffer(s) most
advancedExpressions.example: When budgets are slashed, it is invariably the most vulnerable who suffer most. （强调句式+因果论证，凸显社会关切）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She suffered a lot but did not give up.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Though she had suffered blow after blow — the loss, the loneliness, the endless nights of doubt — she clenched her fists, lifted her chin, and refused to let despair have the final word. （读后续写·坚韧+动作描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Though 让步状语 + blow after blow 反复强调 + 破折号列举三重苦难 + 三个动作(clenched, lifted, refused)递进 + have the final word 拟人

sentenceUpgrade.original: If we ignore the environment, we will suffer.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Should we continue to turn a deaf ear to the cries of our dying planet, it is future generations who will suffer the bitterest of consequences. （议论文·环境·论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Should 引导倒装虚拟条件 + turn a deaf ear to 习语 + the cries of our dying planet 拟人比喻 + it is...who 强调句 + the bitterest of consequences 最高级

original_sentence: Amy misunderstood me.
readingExamples: Amy misunderstood me.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to fail to understand someone or something correctly
(2) vt. to form a wrong idea about a person's words, actions, or intentions
(3) vi. to interpret a situation, statement, or meaning incorrectly

posExamples.sentence: She had misunderstood his silence as indifference, never guessing that behind those quiet eyes lay a love too deep to put into words. （读后续写·误会·情感反转）
I am writing to apologise sincerely, for I now realise that I completely misunderstood your kind intentions at yesterday's meeting. （应用文·道歉信）
People often misunderstand tolerance as weakness, when in truth it takes far greater strength to forgive than to retaliate. （议论文·宽容·论证）
"Don't misunderstand," he said hurriedly, reaching for her hand as she turned to leave, "I never meant to hurt you." （读后续写·澄清·对话）

collocations.example: It pained him deeply to realise that his best friend had misunderstood his intentions all along. （读后续写·友谊·遗憾）
The two nations had completely misunderstood each other's signals, and the crisis deepened with every passing hour. （议论文·沟通·反面例证）
The scientist's revolutionary theory was widely misunderstood in her lifetime and only celebrated long after her death. （议论文·创新·历史例证）
Many students misunderstand the true meaning of success, equating it solely with money and fame. （议论文·价值观）

advancedExpressions.expression: sth. kept eating away at sb., until ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: He felt guilty for a long time and it made him unhappy.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Social media is bad for real friendship.

original_sentence: We may be able to make many friends online, but these friendships can be quite shallow.
readingExamples: We may be able to make many friends online, but these friendships can be quite shallow.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. not having much distance between the top surface and the bottom; not deep
(2) adj. not showing serious or careful thought; concerned only with unimportant things
(3) adj. (of breathing) taking in only a little air with each breath
(4) n. (usually plural: the shallows) an area of water that is not deep

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 浅水处，浅滩(常用复数 shallows)
uncommonMeanings.example: Wading through the sun-warmed shallows, the two children shrieked with delight as tiny silver fish darted between their bare ankles. （读后续写·童年·夏日戏水）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (呼吸)微弱的，短促的
uncommonMeanings.example: The rescued climber lay pale in the snow, his breathing so shallow that for one terrible moment we feared it had stopped altogether. （读后续写·救援·生死一线）

posExamples.sentence: The river here was deceptively shallow, and the little boy waded further and further from the bank, unaware of the sudden drop that waited just ahead. （读后续写·危险·悬念）

For years I dismissed my cousin as shallow and vain, until the day I watched her sit through the night beside a dying stranger's bed. （读后续写·偏见反转·成长）

collocations.example: The old fisherman warned us to keep the boat in shallow water, for the current beyond the reef could sweep a man out to sea in seconds. （读后续写·航海·警告）
They crossed the shallow stream on stepping stones worn smooth by a hundred summers of bare feet. （读后续写·乡村·怀旧）
Curled beneath the blanket, she took quick, shallow breaths, terrified that the slightest sound might give away her hiding place. （读后续写·紧张·躲藏）
It is unfair to write someone off as a shallow person simply because they are cheerful; joy is not the enemy of depth. （议论文·评判他人）
The countless shallow friendships she had collected online melted away the moment she truly needed a shoulder to cry on. （读后续写·友情·幻灭）
Judging people by their looks is a shallow and superficial habit that blinds us to the richness within. （议论文·偏见）

synonyms.example: Her interest in the subject proved superficial, fading the moment the topic demanded real effort. （议论文·学习态度）
synonyms.usage: 书面、正式，强调"只停留在表面、缺乏深度"，多修饰知识、理解、关注；shallow 更口语，也可指物理上的"浅"，形容人时略带贬义

synonyms.example: The committee dismissed his frivolous complaint and turned to matters that truly mattered. （议论文·态度）
synonyms.usage: 强调"不严肃、爱玩闹、缺乏责任感"，语气更重；shallow 侧重"缺乏思想深度"，不一定含"轻浮胡闹"之意

synonyms.example: In the grand sweep of life, the trivial quarrels we cling to today will seem laughably small tomorrow. （议论文·人生感悟）
synonyms.usage: 修饰事物，指"不重要、无价值"；shallow 修饰人或想法时指"没深度"，二者角度不同，不可直接互换

advancedExpressions.expression: deceptively shallow, the ... concealed ...
advancedExpressions.example: Deceptively shallow near the bank, the pool concealed a sudden, treacherous depth that swallowed the sunlight whole. （形容词前置 + conceal 制造隐患，续写危险场景埋伏笔）

advancedExpressions.expression: we should not settle for shallow ..., but seek ...

advancedExpressions.expression: what looks shallow on the surface may hide ...
advancedExpressions.example: What looks shallow on the surface may hide unexpected depths, just as the quietest stream often conceals the deepest current. （表里对比 + 类比升华，反对以貌取人）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The online friendships were not deep and did not last.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Like reflections on shallow water, those online friendships shimmered brightly for a season, then scattered at the first ripple of real trouble, leaving her lonelier than before. （读后续写·友情·幻灭）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 明喻(like reflections on shallow water) + shimmered/scattered 动态对比 + leaving 分词状语收束孤独感

sentenceUpgrade.original: People today have shallow relationships because of the internet.

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: In an era where... 时代背景 + followers rather than friends 词义对比 + 隐喻(wide as an ocean yet...) 生动呈现"广而浅"

original_sentence: Social media like blogs has come between us and the friends whom we love.
readingExamples: Social media like blogs has come between us and the friends whom we love.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a website or webpage on which a person regularly records their opinions, experiences, or information about a particular subject
(2) n. a single entry or post on such a website
(3) vi. to write or maintain a blog; to add new posts to a blog

posExamples.sentence: Every night after her family fell asleep, the shy girl poured her secret dreams into a travel blog, never once imagining that thousands of strangers were quietly reading, and cheering, her on. （读后续写·成长·自我表达）
I am writing to recommend that our school set up an English blog, where students could share book reviews and practise writing for a real audience beyond the classroom. （应用文·建议信）

When the earthquake cut off all phone lines, a teenager's simple blog became the village's only window to the outside world, and messages of hope poured in from across the country. （读后续写·灾难·希望）

collocations.example: For three quiet years she kept a blog about caring for stray cats, and slowly a scattered community of kind hearts gathered around it. （读后续写·善良·联结）
The moment he posted his honest apology on his blog, a wave of forgiving comments reminded him that people are kinder than we fear. （读后续写·和解·温暖）
Her travel blog, rich with vivid photos and heartfelt stories, inspired countless readers to step beyond their own front doors. （应用文·推荐）
Every student who follows the teacher's grammar blog receives one clear, well-chosen writing tip each morning. （应用文·通知）
A single honest blog post about her struggle with anxiety brought hundreds of lonely readers a sudden, healing sense of not being alone. （议论文·分享的力量）
Encouraged by his teacher, the once-silent boy launched a science blog that soon became the talk of the whole grade. （读后续写·自信·蜕变）
However busy she was, she updated her charity blog every Sunday, believing that consistency was itself a form of kindness. （应用文·坚持）

synonyms.example: In her worn leather diary she confided the fears she could never speak aloud, its pages the only listener she fully trusted. （读后续写·心事·私密）
synonyms.usage: 指私人日记，通常不公开、供自己保存；blog 是网络平台上公开或半公开的记录，面向读者、可互动

synonyms.example: The scientist kept a meticulous journal of every experiment, however small the result. （议论文·科学精神）
synonyms.usage: 偏正式，既指个人"日志、随笔"，也指"学术期刊"；blog 特指网络博客，语域更现代、更口语

synonyms.example: Within an hour her heartfelt post had been shared thousands of times across the city. （议论文·信息传播）
synonyms.usage: 指社交平台上的"单条帖子"，可以是文字、图片、视频；blog 通常指持续更新的整个网站，或其中一篇较完整的文章

advancedExpressions.expression: through her blog, sb. found ...

advancedExpressions.expression: I strongly suggest we launch a ... blog so that ...

advancedExpressions.expression: a blog can either ... or ..., depending on ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: She wrote a blog and many people read it.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Blogs and social media affect real friendship.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: For all the closeness they promise, blogs and other social media can quietly slip between us and the friends we love, replacing the warmth of a shared glance with the cold glow of a screen. （议论文·社交媒体）

translation: 损害…之间的关系，离间；妨碍
original_sentence: Social media like blogs has come between us and the friends whom we love. Texting and messaging cannot take the place of face-to-face chatting. "Sharing" our experiences on social media is not enough to express the values which matter most to us. "Liking" our friends' photos online does not develop the connection which we share. To make friends a real part of our lives, we should put down our smartphones and meet them in person.
readingExamples: Social media like blogs has come between us and the friends whom we love. Texting and messaging cannot take the place of face-to-face chatting. "Sharing" our experiences on social media is not enough to express the values which matter most to us. "Liking" our friends' photos online does not develop the connection which we share. To make friends a real part of our lives, we should put down our smartphones and meet them in person.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. v. to damage the relationship between two people; to cause a division or bad feeling between them

posExamples.sentence: For twenty years the two brothers had shared everything, and Amy was determined that no foolish misunderstanding would ever come between them and the bond they had built since childhood. （读后续写·手足·守护亲情）
I sincerely hope this small disagreement will not come between our two clubs and the friendship we have worked so hard to build over the years. （应用文·和解/致歉信）
We must never let the glow of a screen come between us and the loved ones sitting right beside us, for no message can replace the warmth of a face turned toward our own. （议论文·社交媒体·亲情）
Jealousy, that quiet poison, had slowly come between the once-inseparable friends and the trust that had held them together for so many years. （读后续写·友情·裂痕）

collocations.example: She refused to let idle gossip come between two friends who had stood by each other through every storm. （读后续写·友情·坚守）

collocations.phrase: let sth come between sb and sb
collocations.translation: 让某事损害某人之间的关系

collocations.phrase: come between sb and sth (妨碍某人与某物)

collocations.translation: 金钱/嫉妒/距离造成的隔阂

collocations.phrase: refuse to let anything come between

synonyms.example: The cunning rival tried to drive a wedge between the captain and his loyal crew, but their trust proved too deep to break. （读后续写·团队·信任）
synonyms.usage: 比喻性强(wedge 楔子)，特指"蓄意挑拨、制造分裂"，多含恶意；come between 更中性，隔阂可由事物或误会自然造成，未必是故意

synonyms.example: Rumours have a cruel power to set friend against friend, turning yesterday's allies into today's strangers. （议论文·谣言）
synonyms.usage: 强调"使双方对立、敌对"，结果是彼此为敌；come between 侧重"破坏关系、造成疏远"，未必发展到正面冲突

synonyms.example: He never let his hobbies interfere with the duties he owed to his family. （议论文·责任与平衡）
synonyms.usage: 泛指"干扰、妨碍某事顺利进行"，对象多为事情、进程；come between...and... 特指插入"两者之间"造成隔阂或阻隔，结构更固定

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. vowed that nothing would ever come between ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: Social media harms our real relationships.

original_sentence: To make friends a real part of our lives, we should put down our smartphones and meet them in person.
readingExamples: To make friends a real part of our lives, we should put down our smartphones and meet them in person.
definitionEn:
(1) adv. by going somewhere and being present yourself, rather than sending someone else, phoning, or writing
(2) adv. seeing or meeting someone directly, in their actual physical presence (as opposed to on screen, in a photo, or in the media)
(3) adv. done or delivered by oneself, without the help of an agent or intermediary

posExamples.sentence: When the letter finally arrived, she could not bear to reply on paper; she took the first train north, determined to thank the old woman in person and to see, at last, the face behind those years of kindness. （读后续写·久别重逢）
On behalf of the whole class, I would like to invite you to attend our graduation ceremony in person, for no video call could ever convey how much your guidance has meant to us. （应用文·邀请信）

collocations.translation: 亲自见到某人；当面见面

collocations.phrase: collect / pick sth. up in person

collocations.translation: 亲眼所见（对比照片／屏幕）

synonyms.example: The principal personally handed each graduate their diploma, pausing to offer a quiet word of encouragement. （应用文·典礼报道）

synonyms.example: After months of texting, they finally sat down face to face, and the silence between them said more than any message ever had. （读后续写·情感）

advancedExpressions.expression: no screen / message could ever replace the warmth of ... in person

sentenceUpgrade.original: She went to thank the old man herself.
